Chapter Nine: Modeling Prayer—Teaching Children to Pray for Themselves
As our kids grow up, one of the greatest gifts we can give them is the example of a prayerful life. Think about it—when you show your children what it looks like to pray, you’re not just supporting them in the moment. You’re passing down a legacy of faith and resilience that’ll stay with them long after they leave home.
Modeling prayer isn’t just about formal rituals or set times. It’s about weaving prayer into everyday life. Maybe it’s pausing to give thanks before dinner, asking for help when something’s tough, or just expressing gratitude for tiny joys that pop up. Kids notice what we do. So when you pray openly and honestly, you’re inviting them to do the same.
Here are some practical ways to nurture this habit:
First, try praying out loud together. Keep it simple and age-appropriate, making prayer just another part of your daily routines.
Next, encourage your kids to talk to God on their own. Give them space to share what’s on their mind—even the little stuff. Let them know, nothing is too small for God’s care.
And don’t forget to celebrate when prayers are answered. Share those stories, whether it’s a big miracle or a tiny moment of kindness. It helps your kids see that faith really does make a difference in everyday life.
Picture this: before a big test, or maybe a tough conversation, you and your child take a moment to pray together. Over time, these little moments build real confidence and a sense of connection—not just with you, but with a loving God who cares about every detail.
The heart of this chapter is simple. Teaching your children to pray isn’t about getting it perfect or saying the “right” words. It’s about building a relationship, growing trust, and giving them a tool they can carry into every season of life.
